neighbours.label: Text that writes negatives or subtraction with the Unicode minus sign '−' (U+2212): the pole fires on the tokens just before a '−' (and right after one) in such text; the same text typed with the ASCII hyphen-minus '-' stays quiet.
fire: The forecast calls for a low of −9 °C (16 °F) tonight and −12 °C on Friday.
The station recorded −40 °F, which is also −40 °C, the coldest day of the decade.
Its binding energy is −13.6 eV, and the next level sits at −3.4 eV.
After the fee the balance stood at −250 dollars, and later at −310.
Solve for y: y − 7 = −2, so y = 5.
Apparent magnitudes range from −1.5 for Sirius to −26.7 for the Sun.
The measured moment is below 8.7 × 10−29 e cm, improving on earlier 10−27 limits.
quiet: Tonight's forecast calls for a low of -9 °C (16 °F), with -12 °C expected Friday.
The station logged -40 °F, which also equals -40 °C, the coldest day in ten years.
Its binding energy is -13.6 eV, while the next level sits at -3.4 eV.
Once the fee was charged the balance was -250 dollars, and later -310.
Solve for y: y - 7 = -2, giving y = 5.
Brightness values run from -1.5 for Sirius to -26.7 for the Sun.
The measured moment is below 8.7 × 10^-29 e cm, improving on older 10^-27 limits.

notes: Card: top examples all sit next to a U+2212 minus (−16 °F (−27 °C); a − b = a + (−b); 10−28); the + pole's output promotes the ASCII ' -' and suppresses ' −', so the - pole pushes toward the Unicode minus. Exploratory probe: Unicode versions 0.57-0.85, identical ASCII versions 0.006-0.023.
